First, the Multi-Scale Log-Volatility operator detects instantaneous regime shifts in play-calling behavior by normalizing deviations against historical interquartile ranges of log-variance. This isolates true tactical pivots from random noise. Second, these detected anomalies undergo strict econometric stress-testing via the Sherman-Morrison Leave-One-Out gate. By computing exact parameter shifts without full matrix re-inversion, we identify if an apparent edge is merely an artifact of a single high-leverage outlier game. If the leverage exceeds the Ding/FWL thresholds, the feature is vetoed. Third, surviving signals are subjected to Empirical Bayes shrinkage, penalizing effect sizes inversely proportional to their effective signal-to-noise ratio, preventing overfitting in small-sample DFS contexts. Finally, the validated situational priors feed into the Quantal Response Equilibrium simulator. Here, the OC and DC are modeled as bounded-rational agents optimizing over a JEV-derived bimatrix. The integration ensures that every probabilistic output from the GSE engine is simultaneously statistically robust, economically rational, and dynamically calibrated to the current game state.
